text.p: Regional rubber prices are likely to firm slightly this week on the back of pre-Christmas holiday shortcovering before tapering off towards the year-end, traders said on Monday.
"There might be a slight rebound this week if there is some shortcovering ahead of the holidays, which is usually the case," said a Kuala Lumpur-based rubber trader.

"There should be a bit of shortcovering but after the expiry of the December contract in Japan on the 20th, it will taper off and we'll be in for a long vacation," a trader for a Singapore-based U.S. rubber trading company said.
Malaysian traders said the benchmark RSS1 rubber was expected to rise one cent this week and the SMR20 grade would go up between two and three cents.

The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the benchmark RSS1 at Malaysian 315.50 cents a kg and the SMR20 at 303.50 cents a kg, both for January buyer, at the close of the market on Friday.
"This (increase) is likely to happen, even if it's a technical adjustment," said the trader.
Dealers said December was usually a slow month for the rubber market with most overseas consumers going on long holidays.
"I think prices will stay put," a dealer for a Japanese rubber company in Singapore added. "The shortcovering won't be spectacular. As we draw nearer to Christmas, the market will go to sleep."
Supply of latex and raw materials was comfortable despite persistent rains in the past month, said dealers.
Drum latex was being offered by trading houses at 235 cents a kg on Friday.
Thai rubber prices were steady to slightly higher last week despite thin demand as supplies dropped sharply, traders said. Heavy rains in the south cut supplies from the area.
About 62,961 kg of sheet rubber reached the market last week, an 83.5 percent drop from the previous week, auction market sources said.
Traders expect prices, however, to inch up this week.
"The tight supplies and news that Japan rubber stocks at end of November fell should help bouy the prices," said one trader in the Thai town of Hat Yai.

The Thai benchmark RSS3 for January shipment was priced around US$1.23-1.24 a kg FOB Bangkok against $1.23 a kg. STR20 for January shipment was quoted at $1.22-$1.23 a kg FOB Bangkok. Traders said China and Japan entered the market this week but bought only modest quantities of rubber.
"The Japanese may still be in the market, but I don't think China will be aggressive this week," a trader in Singapore said.
In Indonesia, prices of the benchmark tyre-grade SIR20 rubber will probably stay stable this week, while demand was seen to remain poor, dealers said.

"We expect to secure deals involving only around 1,500 tonnes (of rubber) in December, down from a monthly average of 1,800 tonnes this year. As you know, there are only few enquiries these days," one dealer in Padang said.

Dealers said January SIR20 offer prices were at U.S. 55.00-55.50 cents/lb FOB Medan, 54.75-55.25 FOB Surabaya, Padang and Palembang, 54.00-54.50 FOB Pontianak and Jambi, down 0.25-0.50 cents compared to the previous week.
Sentiment on RSS rubber also remained soft, dealers said.
RSS1 was on offer at 126.50 cents/kg FOB Semarang, down from the previous 127.00 cents, but no deals were done so far, a trader in Jakarta said.
Dealers said January SIR3CV FOB Medan was likely to remain on offer at 142 cents/kg, up from the previous 141.
Latex dealers said high amoniac latex was on offer at 2,230 rupiah/kg FOB Medan for January shipments from the previous 2,200 rupiah on expected lower supply in the coming days.
(With contributions from Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia)
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
